graph_anchor.community: Old Copper communities in the western Great Lakes

regions: North America — Lake Superior / western Great Lakes
scope.configuration: Large utilitarian tools forged from native copper; dated organic material remains embedded in some copper artifacts.

population.value: Old Copper communities in the western Great Lakes

evidence.locator: Introduction, Old Copper practice; Results, modeled start and Table 2
evidence.supports: Identifies the large utilitarian tools and reports the model of Old Copper site/tradition beginning at 7520–6180 cal BP (68%).

evidence.locator: Abstract, directly embedded-organic association
evidence.supports: Reports embedded organic dates associated with 15 Old Copper artifacts; does not by itself date each artifact’s manufacture.

graph_anchor.rationale: An approximate historical model of Old Copper practice is used as an explicitly probabilistic entry proxy; it is not a hard upper or lower date and does not use the modern excavation date.
graph_anchor.uncertainty: Bebber et al. report a 68% credible interval for a modeled onset, so a real onset may lie outside either limit. Associations and individual artifact manufacture dates remain uncertain; the interval is not a known-by claim.
graph_anchor.proxy_justification: Entry is inferred from dated copper-bearing archaeological contexts using a statistical model. This is a 68% credible interval for a modeled onset, not a certain historical date, hard bound, direct first artifact, or proof of the age of each embedded organic sample.

anchor_decisions.review_note: 68% modeled onset range, not hard known-by; chronology depends on archaeological association and Bayesian model assumptions.
